newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise modestly after ambiguous economic data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise modestly after ambiguous economic data.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose in subdued trading Thursday as investors weighed ambiguous economic data.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 17.30 points at 7,303.46. In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a thin margin on modest volume of 259 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 12.26 points to 1,347.81, powered by gains in technology stocks.
"Trading is choppy," one trader said. "For the past two days we've been unchanged and the market looks tired to me."

Financial markets fell initially after the government reported that the core rate of inflation -- excluding the volatile food and energy sector -- in the Consumer Price Index for April rose 0.3 percent, which exceeded Wall Street's forecasts.
The overall CPI was up 0.1 percent last month, matching the 0.1 percent rise in March.
Economists had predicted the overall index would rise by 0.1 percent, but economists had expected the core rate to climb by just 0.2 percent.
Industrial production was unchanged, compared with economists' forecast for a rise of 0.2 percent, and capacity utilization was 83.4 percent, against a forecast of 84.1 percent.

The retail inflation numbers came one day after the government reported surprisingly good news on wholesale prices, as the Producer Price Index for April posted its biggest drop in nearly four years, falling 0.6 percent.
The conflicting data sent mixed signals as to whether the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates at next Tuesday's policy-setting meeting.

"Bonds firmed after the data was released," said Harvey Hirshhorn, chief economist and investment strategist at Stein Roe. "Production was a bit softer and the (new jobless) claims drop was bigger, so it's a mixed bag for markets..."

In another report, the government said fewer Americans entered unemployment lines for the first time in the week ended May 10. First-time jobless claims fell to 319,000 from 350,000 in the previous week.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 5/32, raising its yield to 6.90 percent from Wednesday's 6.88 percent. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.
Robert von Pentz, a managing partner at Columbia Partners, said, "We've come a long way since last month so it's logical to expect some correction."
But if markets felt the Fed would delay a rate hike, stocks would rise, he said.
"Investors are already trading in anticipation of next Tuesday's Fed meeting, as people place their bets on the direction of rates the next few days," Hirshhorn said.
Technology stocks were big gainers, led by Intel Corp., which was hit recently by concerns about a patent infringement lawsuit. Intel climbed 4-1/2 to 157-3/8.
Other high technology companies were also strong, as Microsoft Corp. rose 1-3/8 to 117-1/4, and Oracle Corp. gained 1-9/16 to 45-7/8.
Gateway 2000 Inc. jumped 4-1/8 to 65-1/2 after it said that it would split its shares.
